newsitem.title: USA: Most US debt futures end up, bond down after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Most US debt futures end up, bond down after FOMC.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures ended higher after the Federal Reserve's policy arm left short term rates unchanged, but the June T-bond closed down slightly.
The federal funds target was left at 5.50 percent.
The short end remained buoyed by the news the Fed was standing pat on rates, but an initial rally in the long end quickly faded.
June T-bond futures rallied to 110-12/32 in fast market trade and then slipped into negative territory. Still, the morning low of 109-13/32 was not challenged again.
December Euros rallied to last week's 93.77 high.
Euros remained firm even as T-bonds eroded, and one Euro trader pegged further resistance at 93.84. But he said much more upside could be tentative.
"The general premise is if they don't do it now they'll do it in July," he said.

It was just such a premise that traders said yanked June T-bonds so quickly from their session high. That, and the idea among some that "the Fed is not staying ahead of the ball in terms of inflation," another Euro trader said.
A T-bond trader called it "shocking" that June eroded so quickly from its post-FOMC high.

But he and several other traders noted that June T-bonds remain within last week's range, unable to forge any new ground. Traders noted that both minor support at 109-12/32 and resistance at 110-12/32 held.
"A lot of people expected to see either the 108-00 or the 111-00 handle today and it just wasn't even close to that," the bond trader said. He called 109-20/32 to 25/32 an apparent high volume area.
Kurt Fraim, a futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston, noted the tight ranges in June bonds and notes and said the market showed "not a lot of significance on a closing basis."
"They stayed well within their range," Fraim said.

Jitters before the FOMC meeting weighed on debt futures most of the session, with shorts flattening their positions just before the results. Traders said the market had been evenly divided over whether the Fed would raise rates 25 basis points or leave them unchanged.
Traders said informal polls on the bond futures floor now showed a 60 percent chance of a rate hike in July.

At the close, June T-bonds were down 2/32 to 109-27/32, T-notes rose 3/32 to 107-11/32, muni-bonds rose 5/32 to 116-22/32, Sept T-bills rose 0.055 to 94.540, and December Eurodollars were up 0.060 at 93.735.
